title: Sender-side claim_seq counter: persisted atomic increment-before-claim (Rust+Python library leg)
description: Child of l1qw.20 (sender leg, Rust+Python). No production slot-claim sender exists in any stack today (encode_cose/sign_slot_claim have test-only callers), so this lands the library machinery: a persisted, crash-atomic claim_seq counter (increment, persist, THEN sign) per Mark's l1qw.20 note 'wraps {iid, superframe, seq, slots} in COSE_Sign1, atomically increments seq in NVS before signing'. Rust: persist alongside the existing sealed coordinator state pattern (resources.rs save_coordinator_state_atomic) or a sibling store; expose next_claim_seq() and use it in SlotClaim::encode_cose callers/tests so seq always comes from the counter. Python: assemble the full COSE_Sign1 envelope (decode_cose exists; no encoder today) + file-backed atomic counter. Spec/08 persistence table rows 'Before claim'/'Gateway boot'. Wiring into a live POST path stays blocked on ljgs (SCHC frame budget); note that in the close reason.
